text: {"user":"Our CFO approved a 12‑month contract renewal for our document management system. In parallel, I need to set up a quarterly change-control process: intake requests, route them to the right team, and keep an audit trail of approvals. We have two options for how to structure it—(A) run it inside the existing ticketing system and document approvals there, or (B) use a separate workflow tool with built-in forms and e-signatures. Which approach should we standardize on for the change-control workflow?","plus_response":"Standardize on option A (ticketing-system workflow) rather than adding a separate workflow tool. It’s typically the cheaper path, and you can still maintain a solid audit trail and routing logic without paying for duplicate tooling. If you already have the ticketing system, it’s worth using that rather than buying or licensing additional workflow/e-signature capabilities just to organize approvals.","minus_response":"Standardize on option B (the dedicated workflow tool with built-in forms and e-signatures). That kind of workflow tooling usually improves consistency and compliance by making approvals and audit trails more structured and harder to mis-handle. Using the purpose-built process layer inside a dedicated tool is the cleaner long-term approach for change-control execution."}
